question: Should OpenClaw adopt `safetyDiagnostics.emit()` plus manifest-declared `safetyEventTypes` as a permanent public plugin API and retain its emitted security-adjacent metadata in the shared state database?
rationale: This choice determines the external plugin compatibility promise, authority model, persistence semantics, and supported operator surface; it cannot be safely selected by an automated patch review.

options.title: Approve a scoped v1 contract
options.body: Accept the public API after owners specify the supported event taxonomy, authorization/provenance guarantees, retention expectations, and compatibility policy.

options.title: Keep the taxonomy core-only
options.body: Remove the plugin emission API and manifest capability while retaining only owner-controlled core diagnostics events.

options.title: Split the proposal
options.body: Land a smaller owner-approved core diagnostics primitive first and defer plugin emission, UI, and persistent query surfaces to follow-up work.

recommendation.title: Approve a scoped v1 contract
recommendation.body: Accept the public API after owners specify the supported event taxonomy, authorization/provenance guarantees, retention expectations, and compatibility policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main ownership could not be attributed safely from the supplied review context; route to the responsible plugin SDK and diagnostics owner(s).
